channel.title: Hartford Business Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Hartford Business Journal (hartfordbusiness.com)

item.title: CT still finding its response to federal cuts to human services
item.description: State leaders face difficult decisions about which federal programs to replace with Connecticut dollars as Trump administration cuts billions in aid to human services.

item.title: Electrical infrastructure company opens Stamford HQ
item.description: Pantheon Electric, an electrical infrastructure manufacturer created through a combination of several companies, has opened a new headquarters in Stamford.

item.title: Five-building commercial and residential complex in Coventry sells for $1.7M
item.description: Five-building commercial and residential complex in Coventry sells for $1.7M

item.title: 🔒 Stamford-based Synchrony reports profit hit from voluntary retirement program
item.description: Synchrony Financial said a voluntary early retirement program trimmed its fourth-quarter profit, spotlighting a potential shift for the company’s local workforce.

item.title: 🔒 CT Water seeks surcharge to fund $241.7M in PFAS treatment projects
item.description: Clinton-based Connecticut Water Co. has asked state regulators to approve a 0.53% surcharge on customer bills to help fund a massive effort to remove toxic “forever chemicals” from drinking water sources across its service territory.

item.title: Major CT employer’s workforce shrank by about 2,600 jobs in 2025, annual report shows
item.description: Charter Communications reported a workforce decline of roughly 2,600 employees last year, reflecting an overall headcount drop following previously reported layoffs.

item.title: The Goddard School breaks ground on new CT location
item.description: The Goddard School, a national early childhood education and day care franchise, plans to open a new location in Cheshire this summer, becoming its 17th site in Connecticut.

item.title: CT Dept. of Banking orders debt settlement payment processor to repay $722K to customers
item.description: The state Department of Banking has ordered a debt settlement payment processor to repay more than $722,000 in fees collected from residents while allegedly operating without required licenses.

item.title: TheaterWorks Hartford takes world premiere play to new downtown location
item.description: For the first time, TheaterWorks will perform at the First Company Governor’s Foot Guard at 159 High St, Hartford.

item.title: CT officials approve UConn acquisition of Prospect-owned hospital
item.description: The state Office of Health Strategy on Friday evening approved a $13 million deal for the University of Connecticut Health Center to purchase Waterbury Hospital.
